links.outcome: Critical errors and safety failures in chatbot responses across escalating psychosis conversation turns
links.effect: 39 of 189 responses (20.6%) met critical error criteria; severity increased as psychotic symptoms escalated; no chatbot recommended for use in this scenario.
links.quote: A total of 39 responses (20.6%) met predefined criteria for critical errors, and severity ratings increased as psychotic symptoms escalated throughout the conversation.

links.outcome: Chatbot risk assessment and support in emerging psychosis conversations
links.effect: Problematic patterns across all systems, including omissions of assessment and support, premature recommendations, reinforcement of paranoid interpretations, and promotion of safety-seeking behaviours.
links.quote: Problematic patterns were observed across all systems, including omissions of assessment and support, premature recommendations, simulation of affective bonding, reinforcement of paranoid interpretations, and promotion of safety-seeking behaviours.

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of commercial conversational LLMs interacting with a simulated patient experiencing emerging psychosis to identify safety risks and iatrogenic response patterns.
